At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

_________

What if we didn’t focus on who you are now, but who you could become?

Are you ready to shape the future? Join us at EY as a Graduate in Technology Risk, starting August 2027. We focus on your potential and provide a supportive environment to enhance your professional and personal skills.

The opportunity: your next adventure awaits

As a Graduate in Technology Risk, you will join our Assurance team and work closely with IT managers, CFOs, CTOs, and CISOs across industries. Our team consists of 35 colleagues with diverse educational and cultural backgrounds.

We are looking for analytical and structured individuals with an interest in IT audits, information security, risk management, and IT strategy. Your work will include:

• 
IT audits and risk assessments: Interview stakeholders, understand business and IT processes, test controls, analyse documentation and data, and contribute to reports and recommendations.

• 
IT General Controls and IT Environment Audits: Evaluate IT controls and identify risks related to financial reporting, compliance, and governance frameworks such as ISO 27001 and COBIT.

• 
Service Provider and Technical Platform Audits: Assess controls across service providers, operating systems, databases, and networks.

• 
Data Protection and Security: Support clients with GDPR compliance, information security assessments, and security maturity evaluations.

• 
Technical Platform Audits: Conduct technical reviews of operating systems, databases, and networks, linking technical aspects to business processes.

• 
Emerging Risk Areas: Work with topics such as AI, cybersecurity, cloud governance, DORA, NIS2, ESG, and third-party risk management.

We offer a range of experiences to help you grow in a personalized manner, fostering a culture of global teamwork. You will be surrounded by dedicated colleagues in an inclusive environment, with opportunities for social events to strengthen team cohesion.

Our internal coaching and training programs will equip you with the skills needed to remain relevant in the future, while you build a network of colleagues and mentors at EY.

To learn more about our various teams within Assurance, please visit our career page.

What we look for

• 
You have a growth-focused mindset. We value how you absorb information, learn and take action just as much as the skills you have gained through education and experience.

• 
You are curious and purpose-driven. You see opportunities rather than obstacles and ask insightful questions that help build a better working world.

• 
You are inclusive. You are actively seeking and valuing diverse perspectives, appreciating differences, and collaborating to create a foundation of safety and trust.

• 
Qualifications:

• 

• You completed your studies in 2026 or are set to graduate in 2027.

• 

• You speak and write English fluently.

• 

• You hold, or expect to complete before joining, a relevant master’s degree within IT, information security, auditing, finance, data science, cybersecurity or a related field. You speak and write both Danish and English fluently, enabling you to communicate clearly with clients and colleagues.

What’s in it for you

• 
An exciting introductory program with all new graduates in the Nordics.

• 
A safe onboarding by your own personal buddy and counselor.

• 
Flexible and hybrid-working conditions, so you can make a meaningful impact, your way.

• 
Highly collaborative teams and great support of a network of knowledgeable colleagues.

• 
Continuous development and opportunities to grow your own career through learnings and experiences. A structured learning journey with on-the-job coaching and opportunities to work toward relevant professional certifications.

What you can expect

If you find this position interesting and recognize yourself in the description above, we would like to hear from you as soon as possible. Application deadline: 15 November 2026.

The steps in our recruitment process are as follows:

• 
Application: Submit your cover letter, CV and most recent grade transcript.

• 
Assessment: After submitting your application, you will receive a link to our assessment within a few days. The assessment takes approximately 20 minutes and must be completed by 18 November.

• 
Video: Following the assessment, you are required to complete a brief video interview consisting of three questions outlining your motivation for this role. You can complete this at your convenience; however, it must be submitted by 22 November.

• 
Interview: Selected candidates will be invited to face-to-face interviews on an ongoing basis.

Please note that only applicants who have completed the assessment and video will be considered for the position. We look forward to receiving your application!

Are you motivated by taking architectural accountability for complex business-critical solutions while shaping architecture across a global manufacturing organisation? If so, you could be our new Domain Architect within Manufacturing Architecture, combining responsibility for a local ERP solution with Domain Architecture leadership across Global Manufacturing & Supply (GMS).

_**The Position

You will serve as the accountable Solution Architect for the Local Manufacturing Tehran (LMT) ERP solution, supporting both the affiliate and manufacturing operations throughout the solution lifecycle. At the same time, you will provide Domain Architecture leadership across GMS by shaping target architecture and architectural guardrails, leading solution reviews and architecture forums, and helping ensure technology decisions support our manufacturing strategy and Enterprise IT direction.

**

• Take accountable Solution Architecture responsibility for the LMT ERP solution throughout its lifecycle, from design and implementation through maintenance and operations, translating business strategies and requirements into scalable architecture and solution designs

• Act as the primary architectural counterpart for the ERP vendor, challenging recommendations where needed and ensuring solutions remain maintainable, compliant and aligned with Novo Nordisk architecture, while ensuring strong collaboration between business stakeholders and external partners

• Communicate complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders and build alignment across functions

• A Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology or a related field

• Extensive experience within Solution Architecture, Domain Architecture, Enterprise Architecture or a related discipline, including architectural accountability for complex enterprise applications or platforms

• Experience working with ERP or similarly complex business-critical enterprise applications and business processes

• Demonstrated ability to influence architecture decisions across multiple functions, stakeholders and technology domains without direct line authority and proven ability to collaborate with vendors and cross-functional teams

• Experience with architecture governance, target architecture, design/solution reviews, architectural standards or similar practices is strongly preferred

• Experience working in regulated environments, preferably within pharmaceuticals, manufacturing or life sciences

• Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities

With customers across military, tactical, emergency, HEMS, and hospital environments worldwide, our ambition is to become the global leader in blood and IV-fluid warming solutions for pre-hospital and through hospital care. Learn more about ˚MEQU: www.mequ.dk

On behalf of ˚MEQU, Best Talent is recruiting an International Product Manager.

The Team

You will join a small, ambitious Marketing team with ambitious plans and great impact on the future growth of the company. Success is driven by close collaboration across Marketing, R&D, QA/RA, Operations, and Commercial functions in a fast moving and highly cross-functional environment.

International Product Manager

Drive global product strategy for an innovative Danish MedTech company

• Shape life-saving MedTech solutions through your clinical expertise

• Collaborate with leading healthcare providers, emergency services, and military organizations

• Play a key role in the international growth of a fast-scaling Danish MedTech company with a meaningful and global purpose

The Role

We are looking for an International Product Manager who can bridge clinical insights, users’ needs, regulatory requirements, and technical development to drive successful global product strategies and commercial execution.

You will own the global product lifecycle across emergency, tactical, and hospital segments. With the United States representing ˚MEQU’s most important growth market, you will play a key role in ensuring that product positioning, roadmap priorities, and value propositions algin with the clinical, regulatory, and commercial requirements of US military, EMS, HEMS, and hospital customers.

Working across the organization, you will ensure that user insights, market needs, engineering priorities and regulatory considerations are translated into clear product direction and commercially viable solutions.

As the internal subject-matter expert within pre-hospital blood and IV transfusion, you will convert clinical challenges into prioritized product requirements that guide product development and long-term portfolio decisions. • Developments in clinical standards of care.

• Tactical and military medical protocols.

• Global procurement and reimbursement structures.

• Competitive and technological developments.

• International market dynamics and commercial opportunities.

• Develop instructions for use, training materials, user guides, and educational content to support sales teams, distributors, and clinical specialists globally.

You bring a clinical background within emergency medicine, pre-hospital care, HEMS, military medicine, or tactical care, combined with hands-on experience with blood and IV transfusion in critical settings. You understand the realities and challenges faced by end users in high-pressure environments.

In addition, you have commercial insight into the MedTech industry and experience supporting product positioning, launches, and international market development. Experience working with institutional customers medical device markets and understand how to position, launch, and scale products internationally. Experience with institutional and public procurement structures is highly valued.

You understand medical device development and the regulatory environment and are able to translate complex clinical needs into structured product requirements that create both customers value and commercial impact.

Your personality – You are:

• A strong communicator with who bridges clinical technical, regulatory, and commercial perspectives.

• Commercially minded with a strategic and customer-centric approach

• Structured and analytical, with the ability to balance long-term strategy and operational execution

• Proactive, self-driven, and comfortable taking ownership in a dynamic scale-up environment

• Curious, collaborative, and motivated by improving patient outcomes through innovation

˚MEQU offers you:

You will gain international exposure across tactical, emergency, and hospital markets and collaborate closely with global distributors, armed forces, and leading healthcare institutions.

• A high-impact position with global strategic product influence

• A dynamic, international, and collaborative work environment

• A diverse team of 30+ colleagues headquartered in Copenhagen

• A mission-driven culture focused on improving patient outcomes

• Competitive salary with a pension scheme and up-to-date benefits

Application:

Please send your application in English, marked ”1947/International Product Manager” to job@besttalent.dk. Interviews will be conducted on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Learn more about Best Talent at www.besttalent.dk.

The Role and Department

Our QC lab is growing in activities and looking to recruit an IT System Administrator to join our team onsite in Ballerup.

As IT system administrator at Genmab, you will provide administrative and developmental support to all our QC IT systems in our Quality Control Laboratory.

The laboratory is responsible for supporting Genmab’s innovative products by performing release and stability testing according to ICH guidelines. Systems are mainly the Labvantage Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS), but also the Empower Chromatography software and additional software controlling analytical equipment.

The role requires a detailed understanding of the LIMS and Empower systems used by QC and its maintenance requirements. The IT system administrator will own the system validation packages, the SOPs, and associated training packages.

The position requires compliance with regulatory requirements to cGMP. Unique to this position is the chance to define the way we work with laboratory IT systems at Genmab.

You will be joining a small team of ambitious and professional colleagues within related fields, who can help you settle into your role, and keep the spirit high while performing the important tasks for our laboratory. The laboratory is newly established, so expect a pioneering atmosphere, where you will help adjust the ways of working in an efficiency oriented direction. We expect you to be ambitious, motivated, self-driven, and to be able to make your colleagues shine in an environment of respectful and flexible collaboration.

You will report to the Associate Director of QC Support, Laboratory systems and Equipment.

Responsibilities

• Liaison between System Users, Application Managers (IT) & QA.

• Drives Business related aspects of system application operations, design, testing, and improvements.

• Manage user access administration and providing initial and on-going training for users.

• Responsible for practical aspects of maintaining the validated state of GxP systems.

• Ensure data integrity and compliance with company SOPs, requirement specifications, and cGMP regulations.

• Load and configure method templates in LIMS and Empower.

• Perform all aspects of QMS processes – Change Control, Deviations, CAPAs – for software used in QC lab.

• Report achievements and escalate issues.

Requirements

•

We are looking for an experienced and commercially minded Service Technology and Automation Lead to modernize our global Customer Service setup. You will drive the implementation of service technology, AI and automation to deliver best-in-class customer experience while improving operational efficiency.

Working closely with Global and Local Service teams, you will optimize processes, develop our global service platform and translate business needs into practical solutions. Your focus will be on increasing efficiency, strengthening service quality and making it easier for customers and partners to do business with us.

**Welcome to Global Sales

**You will join Global Sales, Training and Service within Demant’s Hearing Aids business, where we work to improve the lives of people with hearing loss around the world. We deliver product and sales training, commercial excellence and customer service excellence to our sales companies across Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, the Middle East and Africa, as well as to our independent distributors.

You will become part of our newly established Global Service department, consisting of 14 colleagues. Reporting to the Head of Global Service and joining the Global Service leadership team, you will help define and implement service excellence across our global organization.

**Drive Global Service Efficiency and Automation

**Joining us, you will drive the digitalization of Customer Service through standardized processes, modern technology, AI and automation. You will collaborate with local teams to identify opportunities, develop solutions and ensure successful implementation and adoption.

Success requires a good understanding of Customer Service operations and the ability to use technology to improve efficiency without compromising the personal relationships that underpin great service.

In this role, you will:

• Own and develop Salesforce Service Cloud, including its global rollout, functionality, user experience and roadmap.

• Drive platform adoption and performance, using data and insights to help markets maximize value and identify improvements.

• Implement AI and automation solutions to optimize workflows, improve service quality and increase operational efficiency.

• Define global service standards and guide markets in optimizing technologies such as IVR, workforce management and knowledge repositories.

• Develop customer and partner integrations for larger customers, maintaining the integration roadmap with Global IT.

• Drive stakeholder engagement and implementation, building alignment and momentum across global and local teams.

You can expect approximately 10–20 travel days per year to support our markets and understand local service operations.

**What You Bring

**You hold a relevant commercial master’s degree and ideally have around five years of experience in a similar function, preferably within a larger international organization. You have a track record of improving Customer Service performance and implementing new solutions.

You understand Customer Service at strategic, tactical and operational levels and know how to optimize processes, systems and ways of working. With a good commercial mindset, you recognize how service excellence contributes to customer satisfaction and business performance.

You thrive at the intersection of Customer Service, data, AI and technology. You have experience implementing AI solutions in a business context and translating insights into measurable improvements. Experience with Salesforce Service Cloud, Power BI or similar platforms is an advantage.

jobs.occupation: Two-year postdoc in Computational Lexicography and Linguistics at the Centre for Language Technology, Department of Nordic Studies and Linguistics, UCPH
jobs.description:
The Department of Nordic Studies and Linguistics, Faculty of Humanities, University of Copenhagen (UCPH), Denmark, invites applications for a two-year postdoctoral fellowship in Computational Lexicography and Linguistics to be filled by the 1st of March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The Department of Nordic Studies and Linguistics is home to 1600 students and 160 members of staff. It provides the setting for international research and education from BA to PhD studies within language, language technology, Natural Language Processing, literature, media, culture, and gender studies.

  The successful candidate will be attached to both the Centre for Language Technology (CST), which is one of the research centres of the department, and to the Society of Danish language and Literature (DSL) which compiles and publishes dictionaries and language technology resources for Danish at a scholarly basis, often in research projects in collaboration with CST. The latter affiliation will amount to around six months of the total hiring period of 24 months.

  CST conducts research in different areas of interest for language technology, such as Natural Language Processing, construction of NLP resources, Computational Cognitive Modeling and Multimodality, NLP infrastructure and policy, Representation Learning for NLP and Digital Humanities, among others.  It has a strong international profile, at the same time as pursuing the development of language technology methods and resources for the Danish language. The Centre has considerable experience managing international research projects, frequently attracts visiting researchers, and has organised major conferences in the field. In collaboration with the Department of Computer Science at the University of Copenhagen, it offers an international MSc programme in IT and Cognition. The programme, which currently admits about 30 students a year, comprises a range of courses in Natural Language Processing and Cognitive Science. In addition, we teach at several BA programs and electives, such as the BA ‘Kognitions- and Datavidenskab’ hosted at the Department of Psychology and an elective package on Language-Centric AI for students in the Humanities.

  Job content
 The successful candidate will contribute to the project ELEXAI, which focuses on a European Lexicographic Infrastructure for Artificial Intelligence (https://www.eurac.edu/en/projects/elexai), granted by the European Commission under the Horizon Europe Program.

  The candidate will in particular contribute to the project’s work packages on LLM Benchmarking, the so-called LexBench, which is led by CST and also involves DSL. This part of the project investigates how benchmarks for Natural Language Understanding can be compiled mono- and multilingually from lexical resources and datasets. The position involves designing and compiling such benchmarks in close collaboration with DSL and the other European partners of the project and to apply them in diverse evaluation scenarios. A particular focus will be put on benchmarking word understanding capabilities and on the understanding of figurative language, including the cultural bias that this part of the language may evoke in LLMs.

  Ideal candidates for this work have a background in computational lexicography and/or computational linguistics, with experience in lexicographical work and with good programming skills. It is an advantage although not a requirement, if the candidate has good knowledge of the Danish language.

  Teaching qualifications are not a requirement, since the candidate will not be involved in teaching.

  Qualification requirements
 Applicants will primarily be assessed on their research qualifications, including publications, the ability to conduct independent research and participate in research collaborations, and experience in research management. In addition, the applicant’s research plan and research potential will be assessed in relation to the project described above. 

  Application
 Applications must be submitted online in PDF or Word format. Click on the “Apply now” button at the bottom of this advertisement to apply.

  Applications should be written English and must include the following attachments:  

   	
• Letter of motivation 	
• CV  	
• Documentation of qualifications (exam certificates and PhD diploma)  	
• Complete publication list (attached publications must be marked with an asterisk). The list must be structured systematically and divided into the following categories:    	
• Peer-reviewed publications:  	 		
• Monographs and anthologies 		
• Articles in journals 		
• Book chapters/anthology contributions, etc. 	 	 	
• Non-peer-reviewed publications: 	 		
• Publications disseminating research findings, etc. 	 	   Applicants can attach a maximum of 4 publications. The publication dates must be clearly marked on the list. The selected publications must be uploaded as attachments and numbered [1-4]. 

   	
• Research plan. 	
• Work on the dissemination of research.   Only documentation in English will be assessed.  

  Applicants are invited to familiarize themselves with the faculty’s strategic landmarks here: Strategic landmarks – University of Copenhagen (ku.dk)

  Salary and terms of employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). The salary range starts at DKK 39.993,75 (EUR 5.350,62) + a 18,07% contribution to the pension scheme. It is possible to negotiate salary supplements on an annual basis.

  The recruitment process
 Once the deadline for applications has expired, the Head of Section will consider advice from the appointment committee and select applicants for assessment. All applicants will be notified whether they have been shortlisted. The Head of Section will then set up an expert assessment committee to consider the applications. The selected applicants will be informed who is serving on the committee. They will be offered the opportunity to comment on the committee’s assessment of their application before the appointment is announced.

  Further information on the recruitment process at University of Copenhagen can be found here:  Recruitment process – University of Copenhagen (ku.dk)

  An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc. For more on the diverse working place environment at the University and the University’s participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in Research, see HR Excellence in Research – University of Copenhagen (ku.dk)

  International applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a wide variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about these services as well as information on entering and working in Denmark, here: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen – University of Copenhagen (ku.dk)

  Contact information
 Information about the recruitment process is available from HR SOENDRE, email:HR-SOENDRE@adm.ku.dk, please refer to ID number: 211-2697/26-2L

  Additional information about the position can be obtained from Professor Bolette S. Pedersen, email: bspedersen@hum.ku.dk, The deadline for applications is 13 November 2026, 23:59 [CET] 

  Any applications or additional material submitted after the deadline will not be considered.
